meta.note: UZBEKISTAN, THIRD PASS: THE METADATA SHEETS. RESULT: 12 nodes (4 international hubs, 8 Uzbek indicators), 19 dependencies (18 from the sheets, plus esa-2010 -> un-copni-1999), 2 dropped notes. All 216 English metadata sheets linked from stat.uz's Metadata page were fetched (HTTP 200 each) and searched for named international standards; the round's earlier passes had read ten. The sheets name SNA 2008 in 27, NACE in 29, the UN Principles and Recommendations for a Vital Statistics System in 22 and ICD-10 in 21, among others. Every quote here comes from a sheet's indicator-specific sections (2.1 Concepts and definitions, 2.3.1 Classification, 2.4 Basis for recording, 3.3.2 Other statistical procedures), not the shared governance preamble. Four hubs had no node and were minted from their publishers' own documents: Vital Statistics Revision 3, IRTS 2008, IRES and COPNI. ISCED 2011 could not be verified from UNESCO and is a lead.

reports.title: Principles and Recommendations for a Vital Statistics System, Revision 3
reports.publisher: United Nations Statistics Division (Department of Economic and Social Affairs)
reports.description: The United Nations' standard for registering births, deaths, foetal deaths, marriages, divorces and other vital events and compiling vital statistics from them. Revision 3, Statistical Papers Series M No. 19/Rev.3, adopted by the UN Statistical Commission at its 45th session (2014). Title verified from the publisher's own PDF (unstats.un.org, HTTP 200, 2026-10-24). Minted 2026-10-24 for Uzbekistan's demographic metadata sheets, which name it; a hub for any national vital-statistics release that does.
reports.cadence_note: Not a periodic release: revised roughly once a generation (Revision 2 in 2001, Revision 3 adopted 2014). 0.08 is that interval written as a nominal rate.

reports.title: International Recommendations for Tourism Statistics 2008
reports.publisher: United Nations Statistics Division (Department of Economic and Social Affairs) and World Tourism Organization (UNWTO)
reports.description: The international standard for tourism statistics: visitors, trips, tourism expenditure, tourism industries and their measurement. Statistical Papers Series M No. 83/Rev.1 (ST/ESA/STAT/SER.M/83/Rev.1), drafted by UNWTO in cooperation with the UN Statistics Division. Title verified from the publisher's own PDF (unstats.un.org, HTTP 200, 2026-10-24). Minted 2026-10-24 for Uzbekistan's tourism and trade metadata sheets, which name it.
reports.cadence_note: Not a periodic release: the 1994 recommendations were replaced by the 2008 edition. 0.07 is that interval written as a nominal rate.

reports.title: International Recommendations for Energy Statistics (IRES)
reports.publisher: United Nations Statistics Division (Department of Economic and Social Affairs)
reports.description: The United Nations' recommendations for producing official energy statistics: concepts, classifications, data sources, energy balances and dissemination. Adopted by the UN Statistical Commission at its 42nd session (February 2011) and published as Statistical Papers Series M No. 93 (ST/ESA/STAT/SER.M/93, New York, 2018). Title and series verified from the publisher's own PDF (unstats.un.org, HTTP 200, 2026-10-24). Minted 2026-10-24 for Uzbekistan's electricity metadata sheets, which name it.
reports.cadence_note: Not a periodic release: adopted once (2011), published 2018. 0.05 is nominal, as for SNA 2008.

reports.title: Classification of the Purposes of Non-Profit Institutions Serving Households (COPNI)
reports.description: The United Nations classification of the outlays of non-profit institutions serving households by purpose. One of the four classifications of expenditure according to purpose published together as Statistical Papers Series M No. 84 (ST/ESA/STAT/SER.M/84), with COFOG, COICOP and COPP. UNSD's classification registry records it as operational, adopted 1999 and published 2000 (read 2026-10-24, HTTP 200). Minted 2026-10-24: Uzbekistan's national-accounts sheet names it beside COICOP and COFOG, which closed the `uz-national-accounts -> COPNI` lead.
reports.cadence_note: Not a periodic release. Adopted 1999, published 2000 in Series M No. 84; no later revision is recorded in the registry.

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: RESEARCHED 2026-10-24, closing the second half of the COPNI lead (uz-classifications-2026-09-16.json said 'A COPNI node would also take an in-edge from ESA 2010'). ESA 2010 itself — Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, Annex A — lists COPNI among the functional classifications it uses, ¶23.05, and ¶22.17 says 'For describing and analysing the expenditure of private non-profit institutions serving households, COPNI is used.' ¶23.01 adds that the ESA's classifications are 'fully in line with' COPNI among others. ROUTE: CELLAR's English expression of the act (HTTP 200, 15.8 MB), as the slice's other ESA edges cite; EUR-Lex answers this container HTTP 202 with no body. Quote verbatim from ¶23.05. The act's own text reads 'COFOC' for COFOG in that sentence; the quote keeps it. Grader 2026-10-24 (dry run, --edges, with esa-2010 -> nace-rev2, the other edge citing this document, so its evidence-cache record keeps both): A, quote-found-artefact-named, naming title-run:9/9.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Apart from COFOC and Coicop, the functional classifications include also COPNI (classification of the purposes of non-profit institutions serving households) and COPP (classification of outlays of producers by purpose).

_dropped.edge: (Uzbekistan education statistics, no node) -> ISCED 2011 (no node)
_dropped.why: LEAD, 2026-10-24. Four stat.uz sheets name ISCED: the number of educational institutions (410), teaching staff (411) and admissions to higher education (416) each say their Regulations 'are based on international standards ("International Standard Classification of Education" (ISCED 2011), "Areas of Education and Vocational Training" (ISCED-0 2013) …' prepared by the UNESCO Institute for Statistics, and mean years of schooling (438) converts attainment 'according to ISCED'. No ISCED node exists and none was minted: UNESCO's own title could not be read from this container (uis.unesco.org's ISCED topic page links no document and a guessed PDF path answered 404; unesdoc.unesco.org answered a Cloudflare challenge, which was not worked around).

2026-10-24. About twenty of the 216 stat.uz sheets (fertility, mortality, infant and child mortality, marriages, divorces, arrivals, departures, natural growth, premature births, population density, age distribution) name the same 'Principles and Recommendations for a Vital Statistics System' (Revision 3) in their section 2.1.1. Only population, births and deaths were minted, as the three headline vital statistics; the rest are indicator sheets for the same register and would wire the same way if minted.
